raw_response:
I farm 40 mu with just two people at home, so I will keep the easy, steady land in wheat-maize and leave cotton on a smaller block. That is how I keep the cash flow and labor both under control. I have well irrigation, so I do not want to save too hard on water or fertilizer and then lose yield. In our area, if wheat and maize look weak, the loss is much bigger than the cost of one more topdressing or one more watering. I usually start from what worked before, then adjust a little. This year I will put 30 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 10 mu into cotton. Wheat and maize are my main crops, so I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, give them enough nitrogen, and not short them on potassium the way some old habits do. For wheat, I will aim steady, not extreme, around 14 kg pure nitrogen per mu with 7 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium, and I will water about 3 times if the season is normal. For summer maize on the same 30 mu, I will go a little lighter than wheat on total fertilizer but still enough for a good ear, around 13 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium, with 2 irrigations. Cotton costs more labor and spraying, so I will not spread it too wide with only two people in the house. I will keep cotton at 10 mu, use a better seed, push potassium a bit more, and plan more sprays because once aphids, mirids, or bollworm get ahead, the field is hard to pull back. I would rather spend some money on inputs than watch yield fall in August and regret it later.
